text:
incident-bot: P1 alert — KV cache eviction rate spike detected on cluster=prod, shard-group=12. Evictions/min increased 20x over baseline, p50 latency up 42ms -> 190ms, error rate +3.4% (user-facing timeouts). Paging teams: eng-runtime, eng-sre.

maya: ack. I'm on it — paging sam and rachel for mitigation. Any known deploys?

sam: no deploys in last 30m from infra. Seeing sustained microbatch queue growth and continuous-batching kernel thrash. Related metric: continuous_batching.batch_window_ms distribution shifted right.

maya: sharing quick numbers — last 5m: RPS ~12k, cache hit 62% -> 37%, evict/min 14k -> 280k, avg seq len ~420. Looks like long-tail requests + wide batch windows causing KV cache churn.

alex-ml: adding context: a few customers started long-sequence workloads (chatty evals) which increase KV footprint; continuous batching keeps long-lived KV caches and prevents eviction LRU from stabilizing. We're seeing an amplification loop.

rachel-sre: initial mitigation options: 1) reduce global batch_window_ms to shrink microbatching window, 2) flip continuous_batching flag to 'off' cluster-wide, 3) per-customer override for largest tenants, 4) throttle prefetch/prefill. Prefer a targeted approach first.

maya: agreed. I'd prefer per-customer overrides for top 5 tenants + a 10% canary of the cluster with flag off to validate. If that doesn't stabilize in 5m, reduce batch_window_ms globally.

sam: I can flip per-cust and run a canary. Command I'm going to run:```bash
# turn off continuous batching for zephyr-health (cust-id: zph-233)
flagctl set continuous_batching --customer zph-233 --value false --reason "eviction surge live mitigation"
# canary 10% cluster toggle
flagctl set continuous_batching --scope cluster:prod --value false --canary 10 --reason "eviction surge canary"
```

deployer-bot: flagctl: acknowledged. Canaries queued (id=canary-8812). Patch will apply to 10% of production hosts over the next ~45s.

incident-bot: update: automation detected reduced eviction rate on canary hosts (evict/min down 78% on canary vs +20% baseline). Continue rollout?

rachel-sre: nice. Hold at 10% for 5m and watch tail latency and error rate. Also schedule per-cust protections for top tier (zephyr-health, lumin-data, arcpay).

maya: putting list: zephyr-health, lumin-data, arcpay, novum-ai, infra-sandbox. Sam — please set overrides for those five now.

sam: running:```bash
flagctl set continuous_batching --customer lumin-data --value false --reason "live mitigation"
flagctl set continuous_batching --customer arcpay --value false --reason "live mitigation"
flagctl set continuous_batching --customer novum-ai --value false --reason "live mitigation"
flagctl set continuous_batching --customer infra-sandbox --value false --reason "live mitigation"
```

deployer-bot: per-customer flag updates applied (tx ids: 0x5a2,0x5a3,0x5a4,0x5a5).

maya: after canary hold (5m) — metrics look good: cluster p50 down to 68ms, hit rate recovered to 58%, evictions/min dropping ~65% cluster-wide. Error rate back to baseline.

alex-ml: good signal. Need to decide whether to keep cluster-wide flag off or instead tune batch_window_ms to a smaller value so batching still helps throughput but avoids long KV lives. Tuning keeps cost benefits.

rachel-sre: we should do a gradual hotfix: roll back continuous_batching cluster-wide -> false for next 30m to fully break the amplification, then roll a config change reducing batch_window_ms from 128ms -> 32ms and re-enable continuous_batching behind a canary. That reduces cache pressure while preserving batching benefits.

maya: agreed. Plan: 1) maintain per-customer overrides and extend cluster canary -> 100% (flip off) to stop the surge, 2) push hotfix config: kv.batch.window_ms=32, 3) re-enable continuous_batching via canary. I'll coordinate the canary steps.

sam: executing cluster flip now:```bash
flagctl set continuous_batching --scope cluster:prod --value false --reason "emergency mitigation — eviction surge"
```

deployer-bot: flagctl: cluster toggle queued (id=canary-8812). Rolling to 100% over ~2m.

incident-bot: automation: cluster-wide hosts evict/min dropping 92% after full toggle. User-facing errors dropping.

rachel-sre: excellent. Now let's push the hotfix config. sam, can you send the config patch to config-store and create a canary rollout? Minimal change: kv.batch.window_ms = 32 (was 128).

sam: raised PR #4227 (link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra-config/pulls/4227) with the change. Deploy plan: apply to canary fleet (5 hosts) -> validate -> 25% -> 100%. I'll start canary after approvals.

maya: approvals in flight. While we wait, assess customer impact and comms. Which customers saw timeouts? We have a list: zephyr-health had 82% of timeouts, lumin-data 7%, arcpay 3%, others <1%. Need CX & AE ping for zephyr-health ASAP.

alex-ml: note for postmortem: root cause likely interaction between long-seq workloads + large default batch window + continuous batching retention policy. Need eval harness to surface tail footprint before rollout.

rachel-sre: p1 mitigation success criteria: evict/min <= 2x baseline, p50 latency <100ms, user error delta <0.5%. We're currently at evict/min ~1.3x baseline and p50 ~72ms. Good to move to hotfix rollout.

sam: canary applying config now to 5 hosts. deploy-bot: rollout id=roll-4227-canary.

deployer-bot: rollout started. canary hosts updated in 38s. Health checks passing.

incident-bot: canary signals: hit rate stable, no regressions in tail latency. Proceed to 25%?

rachel-sre: proceed.

sam: promoting to 25% and monitoring.

maya: bringing AEs: @ae-team: heads up—we had transient timeouts for zephyr-health, we've mitigated and applied per-cust overrides. Will follow up with a summary and RCA.

deployer-bot: rollout to 25% complete. Health OK. Rolling to 100% now.

incident-bot: full rollout complete. kv.batch.window_ms set to 32 across prod. continuous_batching re-enable canary will be attempted next.

sam: re-enable continuous_batching behind canary with smaller window:```bash
flagctl set continuous_batching --scope cluster:prod --value true --canary 10 --reason "re-enable after window reduction"
```

deployer-bot: canary id=canary-8821 queued.

incident-bot: early canary signal: no eviction amplification, hit rate stable, latency within target.

rachel-sre: good. Wait 10m. If stable, promote and close P1.

maya: monitoring 10m — all steady. I'll start incident wrap and owner assignment. Postmortem owner: alex-ml. Action items: 1) add guardrail to auto-limit batch_window_ms when per-host KV usage exceeds threshold, 2) improve customer runway detection (warn before long-seq workloads cause eviction), 3) document per-customer override playbook.

alex-ml: ack on postmortem. I'll work with eng-runtime and devex to add sim tests and a QA harness.

rachel-sre: final note: price/cost impact estimate for customers due to reduced batching (higher per-token cost) — we'll include in postmortem. Comms plan to zephyr-health in flight.

maya: closing thread in 30m after final sanity check. Thanks all for quick response :heart:
